'''''Oxalis articulata''''', known as '''pink-sorrel''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''pink wood sorrel''',<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=284829&isprofile=0&|title=''Oxalis articulata'' subsp. ''rubra''|website=Missouri Botanical Garden|access-date=April 20, 2019}}</ref> '''windowbox wood-sorrel''', '''sourgrass''',<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.terrain.net.nz/friends-of-te-henui-group/weeds-by-scientific-names/oxalis-sourgrass.html|title=''Oxalis articulata'' (Pink sorrel)|website=T.E.R.R.A.I.N.|access-date=2019-04-19}}</ref> is a perennial species of flowering plant in the genus ''[[Oxalis]]'' native to Northern Argentina, Southern Brazil and Uruguay.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oxalis articulata Savigny {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:374673-1 |access-date=2025-06-18 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> It has been introduced in Europe in gardens and is now naturalized in these areas.

The plant is susceptible to rust (disease due to the fungus ''[[Puccinia oxalidis]]'').<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tavares|first1=Silvia|last2=Ramos|first2=Ana Paula|last3=Pires|first3=Ana Sofia|last4=Azinheria|first4=Helena|last5=Caldeirinha|first5=Patricia|last6=Link|first6=Tobias|last7=Abranches|first7=Rita|last8=Do Céu Silva|first8=Maria|last9=Voegele|first9=Ralf|date=2014|title=genome size analyses of Pucciniales reveal the largest fungal genomes|journal= Frontiers in Plant Science|volume=5|page=422|doi=10.3389/fpls.2014.00422|pmid=25206357|pmc=4143883|doi-access=free|bibcode=2014FrPS....5..422T }}</ref>

== Description ==
As the name would imply, this species of ''Oxalis'' typically has pink to violet flowers<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Ghahremaninejad|first1=F|last2=Gholamian|first2=F|date=2006|title=A new record (''Oxalis articulata'') from Iran|journal=Iranian Journal of Botany|volume=12|pages=55–56}}</ref> with petals 10–15 mm long. Numerous tufted leaves emerge from the ground in a [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]]. At the end of a long, slender petiole (up to 30 cm), 3 generally orbicular leaflets (5 cm in diameter) spread out perpendicular to the petiole. Each leaflet is obcordate (heart-shaped), with a very finely [[ciliate]]d margin, and a deeply notched apex. The underside of the leaflets generally bears clearly visible orange [[granulation]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Oxalis~articulata|title=''Oxalis articulata'' Savigny|website=PlantNET}}</ref>

This species has "plants arising from a thick, woody, irregularly nodulate-segmented rhizome often with persistent, thickened, and lignescent [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] bases; flowers 3–12 in umbelliform [[cymes]], less commonly in irregular cymes".<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Horne|first1=Howard|last2=Barger|first2=Wayne|last3=Nesom|first3=Guy|date=2013|title=Two South American species of Oxalis (Oxalidaceae) naturalized in Alabama and the USA, first report.|journal=Phytoneuron|volume=54|pages=6}}</ref>

The plant is a perennial and typically grows up to 45 cm tall<ref name=":3" /> and 2 cm in diameter.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Young |first=D |date=1958 |title=Oxalis in the British Isles |journal=Watsonia |volume=4 |pages=51–69}}</ref> It spreads by [[rhizome]]s (up to 15 cm<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Oxalis+articulata|title=''Oxalis articulata''|website=Useful Tropical Plants|access-date=April 18, 2019}}</ref>) to form colonies.<ref name=":0" /> It is [[hermaphrodite]] and also infrequently produces seeds in long, cylindrical capsules.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldsun.com/living/article142874129.html|title=Mystery Plant: ''Oxalis articulata''|last=Nelson|first=John|date=April 5, 2017|website=The Herald Sun|access-date=April 19, 2019}}</ref>

== Uses ==
''Oxalis articulata'' can be used as [[groundcover|ground cover]] in green zones to inhibit the growth of weeds in such areas and alleviate the need for herbicide. This is due to the allelopathic leachates in the leaves and exudates from the roots of living Oxalis plants which display significant inhibitory activities on the growth of other plants.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shiraishi|first1=Sakaya|last2=Watanabe|first2=Izumi|last3=Kuno|first3=Katsuji|last4=Fujii|first4=Yoshiharu|date=2005|title=Evaluation of the allelopathic activity of five Oxalidaceae cover plants and the demonstration of potent weed suppression by Oxalis species|journal=Weed Biology and Management|volume=5|issue=3|pages=128–136|doi=10.1111/j.1445-6664.2005.00167.x|bibcode=2005WeeBM...5..128S }}</ref> Oxalate extracts from the leaves have been shown to exhibit anti-fungal properties.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shiraishi|first1=Sayaka|last2=Watanabe|first2=Izumi|last3=Kuno|first3=Katsuji|last4=Ishii|first4=Hideo|last5=Fujii|first5=Yoshiharu|date=2003|title=Soil drenching with water extracts of ''Oxalis articulata'' Savigny suppress Fusarium wilt of tomato.|journal=Weed Biology and Management|volume=3|issue=3|pages=184–188|doi=10.1046/j.1445-6664.2003.00102.x|bibcode=2003WeeBM...3..184S }}</ref>

''Oxalis articulata'' has a large amount of ascorbic acid and is eaten as a vegetable by inhabitants of [[Jharkhand|Jharkhand, India]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Gupta|first1=Sakshi|last2=Srivastava|first2=Anuradha|last3=Lal|first3=Eugenia|date=2017|title=Food and Nutritional Security through wild edible vegetables and weeds in two district of Jharkhard, India|journal=Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry|volume=6|pages=1402–1409}}</ref>

=== Cultivation ===
''Oxalis articulata'' is used as an ornamental in China.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=LY|last2=Jin|first2=FM|last3=Jin|first3=YJ|last4=Xui|first4=JQ|last5=Wen|first5=W|last6=Chen|first6=JH|last7=Ye|first7=D|date=February 2018|title=Responses of underground clonal storage to mowing of the alien clonal weed species ''Oxalis articulata''|journal=Yingyong Shengtai Xuebao|volume=29|issue=2|pages=501–506|pmid=29692064|doi=10.13287/j.1001-9332.201802.004}}</ref> The plant is not drought tolerant and soil should be kept moist. It grows best in acid or light soils. ''Oxalis articulata'' is more competitive than other species in this family, and can tolerate plant beds which are loosely populated with other greenery. However, it thrives in disturbed ground.<ref name=":2" /> Though it is hardy, it grows best in warmer areas.<ref name=":2" /> It flowers continuously from throughout the warmer months and goes dormant at first frost.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=JÁNOS|first=ÁGOSTON|date=2016|title=Investigation of the ornamental value of Bulbous Oxalis species and cultivars|journal=Lucrări Ştiinţifice|volume=1|pages=5–10}}</ref> Out of the sun, the flowers roll up into a tube-like shape.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wildflowerfinder.org.uk/Flowers/S/Sorrel(Pink)/Sorrel(Pink).htm|title=Pink-Sorrel, ''Oxalis articulata''|date=2016|website=Wild Flower Finder|access-date=April 20, 2019}}</ref> It is extensively naturalized in southeastern Australia, particularly in the crescent-shaped, temperate strip from [[South Australia]] to southeastern [[Queensland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/media/Html/oxalis_articulata.htm|title=Oxalis articulata|date=2016|website=Lucid Central.org|access-date=June 21, 2025}}</ref>

== Control ==
It is regarded as a weed in many places, including South Australia, New South Wales, and Victoria.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/media/Html/oxalis_articulata.htm|title=''Oxalis articulata'' Savigny|website=Queensland Government|access-date=April 19, 2019}}</ref>  As it spreads through rhizomes, care should be taken when removing to avoid leaving behind bulbs. Digging the bulbs out while soil is moist when removing can help this process.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.esc.nsw.gov.au/living-in/living-sustainably/introduced-plants-and-animals/weeds/weed-profiles/wood-sorrel-oxalis-articulata|title=Wood-sorrel (''Oxalis articulata'')|website=Eurobodalla Shire Council|access-date=April 20, 2019}}</ref>
